papers.title: Improving Adaptivity via Over-Parameterization in Sequence Models

summary.en: In a sequence model, learning coordinate scales can adapt to the signal and improve rates over fixed scales, with suitable initialization and early stopping.
summary.zh: 在序列模型中，通过学习坐标尺度适应信号结构；在适当初始化与早停条件下，相比固定尺度方法改善收敛速率。

papers.title: Diagonal Over-parameterization in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces as an Adaptive Feature Model: Generalization and Adaptivity

summary.en: A diagonal adaptive kernel learns eigenvalue weights and output coefficients together. The analysis connects feature adaptation, generalization and depth in RKHS regression.
summary.zh: 对角自适应核同时学习特征值权重与输出系数，在 RKHS 回归中分析特征适应、泛化能力和参数化深度之间的关系。

papers.title: Supporting Evidence for the Adaptive Feature Program across Diverse Models

summary.en: The Feature Error Measure (FEM) combines representation and statistical considerations. Specific diagonal and directional models provide evidence that training can improve feature quality under the paper’s assumptions.
summary.zh: Feature Error Measure（FEM）结合表示能力与统计误差。在论文假设下，对角及方向自适应模型为训练改善特征质量提供了理论支持。

papers.title: Alignment-Sensitive Minimax Rates for Spectral Algorithms with Learned Kernels
papers.authors: Dongming Huang · Zhifan Li · Yicheng Li · Qian Lin

tag.zh: 对齐关系与统计复杂度

summary.en: Effective Span Dimension (ESD) measures complexity through the target, spectral order and noise. The work relates alignment to minimax risk and studies when spectral learning reduces this complexity.
summary.zh: 有效跨度维数（ESD）结合目标信号、谱排序与噪声衡量复杂度，将对齐关系联系到极小极大风险，并分析谱学习何时能降低这一复杂度。

papers.title: Risk Equivalence between RKHS Regression and Sequence Models for Lipschitz Spectral Algorithms
papers.authors: Yicheng Li · Yuqian Cheng · Zhuo Chen · Qian Lin

summary.en: Under the stated spectral, sample and filter conditions, RKHS spectral-regression risk is asymptotically equivalent to the corresponding Gaussian sequence-model risk.
summary.zh: 在相应谱、样本及滤波条件下，建立 RKHS 谱回归风险与对应高斯序列模型风险的渐近等价关系。

en.title: Adaptive Feature | Qian Lin & Collaborators
en.description: An iterative research program linking abstract feature-map families, fixed, local and global analysis, neural-network feedback, and generalization.
en.hero_title:
From feature families
to how networks learn.
en.hero_intro: Study learning in abstract models. Return to concrete networks for feedback. Refine the assumptions, and work towards a connection between feature formation, training dynamics and generalization.
en.idea_title:
Begin with a family
of feature-map regressions.
en.idea_intro: The starting point is a family of possible feature maps. Each map, together with output coefficients, defines a regression model. This common language lets us study different learning dynamics before specializing to a concrete neural network.
en.equation_caption: Φ maps inputs into a feature space; β supplies the output coefficients. The choice of family is a modeling hypothesis to be refined through the research cycle.
en.lab_title: Try one small model of the framework.
en.lab_intro: The diagonal sequence model holds a basis fixed and learns its coordinate scales. Expand the illustration to compare fixed and adaptive feature dynamics.
en.lab_note: This deterministic, finite-dimensional illustration is inspired by the sequence-model paper. It is not a reproduction of its experiments or a guarantee about neural networks. Late fitting can also learn noise.
en.methods_intro: We observe z = θ* + ε in six coordinates, using fixed synthetic noise. The initial weights are λ = (1, 0.55, 0.25, 0.10, 0.04, 0.015).
en.methods_end: The adaptive model uses θj = ajβj, aj(0) = √λj and βj(0) = 0. The scalar equation follows from a² − β² = λ. Curves use fourth-order Runge–Kutta integration; MSE is evaluated against the known synthetic truth, not against the noisy observations.

en.research_intro: From tractable models to representation measures and fine-grained risk, these works supply different tools and entry points for the program.
en.limits_title: From specific results to a broader theory
en.limits_body: A result for one feature-map family does not settle the full program. Relating abstract dynamics to concrete architectures, testing the assumptions and connecting the resulting trajectories to generalization remain part of the research cycle.

Associate Professor
Department of Statistics and Data Science
Tsinghua University
en.about_body: Qian Lin is an Associate Professor in the Department of Statistics and Data Science at Tsinghua University. With Yicheng Li and other collaborators, he studies statistical learning theory, feature learning and the mathematical foundations of deep learning. Full authorship appears in the paper entries.

en.dynamics_title:
From a given representation
to its formation.
en.dynamics_intro: Fixed, local and global analyses address different questions. Together they help us understand the statistical quality of features and how that quality changes during training.

dynamics.label: Fixed / static
dynamics.title: Characterize learning with a given representation.
dynamics.body: Hold a feature map fixed and analyze how the target, spectrum, noise and estimator jointly determine prediction risk. Fine-grained risk, ESD and FEM provide tools for evaluating representations.
dynamics.question: How should we evaluate a representation, separating target alignment, spectral complexity and the estimator’s role?
dynamics.focus: Target regularity · kernel spectrum · regularization and stopping · noise
dynamics.caption: Regression and risk under fixed features provide a reference for studying dynamic representations.

dynamics.label: Local
dynamics.title: Examine how features and coefficients interact.
dynamics.body: Study changes and responses near a current state, including the joint variation of spectral directions, spectral weights and prediction coefficients under nonlinear parameter coupling.
dynamics.question: How do local changes affect feature quality and risk, and when are local approximations valid?
dynamics.focus: Spectral perturbations · parameter coupling · local approximation · sample dependence
dynamics.caption: Nearby variations help isolate local mechanisms of feature learning.

dynamics.label: Global
dynamics.title: Understand how beneficial features form and persist.
dynamics.body: Follow the joint trajectory of features and coefficients. Study when initialization, parameterization and training mechanisms favor feature formation, and whether those features persist through later training.
dynamics.question: How can local mechanisms inform an account of the whole training process and its generalization?
dynamics.focus: Initialization · training mechanisms · parameterization depth · early stopping
dynamics.caption: Place local mechanisms within the full trajectory to study their longer-term statistical effects.

en.cycle_intro: The abstract theory and concrete neural networks inform one another. Network behavior helps determine which assumptions capture learning, which need revision, and what the next abstract model should retain.
cycle_steps: State the structure and assumptions that make the regression family meaningful and analyzable.
Develop fixed, local and global descriptions, and identify the questions they can answer.
Establish the correspondence for a chosen architecture and training setting; compare the theoretical picture with network behavior.
Identify agreements, gaps and missing structure. Refine the feature-map family and return to the analysis.
en.cycle_return: Each round of feedback informs the next family of assumptions.
en.goal_title:
Connect how a network learns
with how it generalizes.
en.goal_body: Through repeated abstraction, analysis and feedback, work towards an explanation of how neural-network dynamics shape generalization. The aim is a theory whose assumptions are informed by the networks it seeks to explain.
en.goal_note: This is the program’s guiding objective; individual results apply to the models and assumptions stated in each work.
en.hero_note:
How do features that support
generalization form and persist?
en.framework_title: An ongoing dialogue between theory and networks.
en.board_definition: Φ maps inputs into a feature space; β supplies the output coefficients. Structural assumptions on the family 𝓕 are refined through the research cycle.
en.board_tools: Fine-grained risk · ESD / FEM · Tractable models
en.board_return_detail: Refine the feature-family assumptions and analyze again
en.feedback_intro: A concrete correspondence makes three observations useful: how representations change, what they predict after refitting, and how the original network generalizes. These observations guide model refinement and test theoretical conditions.
feedback_items: Track feature spectra and empirical target-alignment measures during training; compare the observed changes with the theoretical picture.
Freeze a learned representation and fit a predictor on independent samples to evaluate the predictions those features can support.
Examine performance on new data alongside representation measures and refitting results to connect feature learning with the original training process.
en.feedback_note: Initial experiments with fully connected, convolutional and residual networks provide observations for this process. The three evaluations address different objects and should be interpreted together.
en.feedback_return: Observe behavior → test theoretical conditions → refine assumptions
en.agenda_title:
Use established tools
to explore the next questions.
en.agenda_intro: Results in specified models offer starting points for a more general analysis of dynamic representations, nonlinear coupling and the conditions for beneficial feature formation.
established_items: Learning curves, optimality, high-dimensional rates, saturation and risk equivalence for fixed representations.
Effective Span Dimension (ESD), Feature Error Measure (FEM), and the role of target alignment.
Over-parameterized sequence models, diagonal adaptive kernels and specific directional models.
questions_items: Handle spectral perturbations and the dependence of trained representations on the sample.
Understand when local approximations apply and how they may translate into generalization gains.
Formation and retention of useful features
Analyze the conditions induced by common initializations and concrete training mechanisms.
en.agenda_note: Existing results hold for their stated models and assumptions; the second column sets out further research directions.

regression_definition.intro: Start with a candidate family 𝓕 of feature maps. Choosing a map Φ and output coefficients β specifies a regression function.
regression_definition.formula_aria: f sub Phi beta of x equals the inner product of Phi of x and beta in feature space H; Phi belongs to family F and beta belongs to H.
terms: The candidate feature-map family, with Φ : 𝓧 → 𝓗.
The representation of input x in feature space 𝓗.
Output coefficients that combine features into a scalar prediction via an inner product.
regression_definition.bridge: The static view fixes Φ; the local view studies nearby changes; the global view follows the joint evolution of Φ and β.

zh.title: Adaptive Feature | 林乾与合作者的研究纲领
zh.description: 从抽象特征映射族出发，通过固定、局部和整体分析，与神经网络实验反复对话，探索特征形成、训练动力学与泛化能力的联系。
zh.eyebrow: ADAPTIVE FEATURE · 自适应特征研究纲领
zh.hero_title:
从特征映射族，
理解神经网络。
zh.hero_intro: 在抽象模型中研究学习，再从具体网络中获得反馈。反复修正假设，逐步建立特征形成、训练动力学与泛化能力之间的联系。
zh.byline: 林乾与合作者 · 清华大学
zh.figure_label: 抽象模型 ↔ 具体神经网络
zh.idea_title:
先考虑一族
抽象的特征映射回归。
zh.idea_intro: 研究的起点是一族可能的特征映射。每个映射与输出系数共同定义一个回归模型。在这一统一语言中分析不同的学习动力学，再与具体神经网络建立对应。
zh.equation_caption: Φ 将输入映射到特征空间，β 给出输出系数。对特征映射族的选择与假设，在后续研究循环中不断修正。
zh.lab_title: 把抽象框架放进一个小模型。
zh.lab_intro: 对角序列模型固定基函数、学习坐标尺度。展开示例，比较固定特征与自适应特征的动力学。
zh.toy_label: 六维序列模型 · 教学示例
zh.lab_note: 这是依据序列模型论文构造的确定性有限维教学示例，并非论文实验的复现，也不是对一般神经网络的性能保证。训练后期也可能拟合噪声。
zh.methods_intro: 在六个坐标上观测 z = θ* + ε，使用固定的合成噪声。初始权重为 λ = (1, 0.55, 0.25, 0.10, 0.04, 0.015)。
zh.methods_end: 自适应模型使用 θj = ajβj，初始 aj(0) = √λj、βj(0) = 0。标量方程由守恒关系 a² − β² = λ 得到。曲线采用四阶 Runge–Kutta 方法计算；均方误差相对于已知的合成真实信号计算，而不是相对于含噪观测。
zh.methods_source: 序列模型论文第 3.1 节

预测器如何在给定表示下学习，又如何与表示共同演化？
zh.dynamics_title:
从给定表示，
到表示的形成。
zh.dynamics_intro: 固定、局部与整体分析关注不同的问题，共同帮助我们理解特征表示的统计质量及其随训练发生的变化。

dynamics.label: 固定 / 静态
dynamics.title: 给定表示，刻画学习难度。
dynamics.body: 从固定特征映射出发，分析目标信号、谱结构、噪声与估计方法如何共同决定预测风险。精细风险、ESD 与 FEM 为比较表示质量提供工具。
dynamics.question: 怎样评价一个表示？目标匹配、谱复杂度与估计方法分别起什么作用？
dynamics.focus: 目标正则性 · 核谱 · 正则化与早停 · 噪声
dynamics.caption: 在给定特征下研究回归与风险，为分析动态表示建立参照。

dynamics.label: 局部
dynamics.title: 考察表示与预测系数的耦合。
dynamics.body: 在当前状态附近研究特征的变化与响应，关注谱方向、谱权重和预测系数的共同变化，以及一般非线性参数耦合下的学习机制。
dynamics.question: 局部变化怎样影响表示质量与预测风险？近似在什么条件下有效？
dynamics.focus: 谱结构扰动 · 参数耦合 · 局部近似 · 样本依赖
dynamics.caption: 从邻域中的变化出发，辨析特征学习的局部机制。

dynamics.label: 整体
dynamics.title: 理解有利特征的形成与保持。
dynamics.body: 沿训练轨迹追踪特征与系数的共同演化，研究初始化、参数化和训练机制何时有利于特征形成，以及这些特征能否在后续训练中保持。
dynamics.question: 怎样从局部机制走向整体训练分析，并与泛化能力建立联系？
dynamics.focus: 初始化 · 训练机制 · 参数化深度 · 早停
dynamics.caption: 把局部机制放回整个学习过程，考察其长期统计作用。

zh.cycle_kicker: 03 / 理论与神经网络的往返
zh.cycle_intro: 抽象理论与具体神经网络相互启发。网络中的行为帮助我们判断哪些假设抓住了学习的关键、哪些需要修正，以及下一轮抽象应当保留什么结构。
cycle_steps: 提出特征映射族与假设
明确回归模型族的结构，提出使它有意义、可分析的假设。
研究固定、局部、整体动力学
在统一框架下建立不同尺度的动力学描述，明确各自能够回答的问题。
在选定的网络结构与训练设置中建立对应，比较理论图景与网络行为。
从网络反馈中修正假设
识别吻合之处、差异与缺失的结构，修正特征映射族，再回到动力学分析。
zh.cycle_return: 每一轮反馈，都成为下一轮假设的依据。
zh.goal_title:
建立神经网络动力学
与泛化能力的联系。
zh.goal_body: 通过反复的抽象、分析与反馈，逐步解释神经网络的学习动力学如何影响泛化能力，让理论中的假设不断受到具体网络行为的检验与修正。
zh.goal_note: 这是研究纲领所追求的目标；各项具体结果的适用范围由相应论文中的模型与假设决定。
zh.hero_note:
有利于泛化的特征，
如何在训练中形成并保持？
zh.framework_title: 抽象与具体，在循环中相遇。
zh.board_definition: Φ 将输入映射到特征空间，β 给出输出系数；映射族 𝓕 的结构假设随研究逐步修正。

zh.feedback_title:
让网络中的观察，
反过来检验理论。
zh.feedback_intro: 在具体网络中建立对应后，需要分别观察表示的变化、表示的预测能力与原网络的泛化表现，再用这些证据提炼模型、检验条件并修正假设。
feedback_items: 特征谱与经验目标匹配
记录训练中的特征谱与经验匹配指标，观察表示怎样变化，以及这些变化是否与理论预期一致。
冻结训练中获得的特征，在独立样本上重新拟合预测器，考察所学表示能够支持怎样的预测。
考察原网络在新数据上的表现，与表示评价及重拟合结果对照，理解特征学习与整体训练的关系。
zh.feedback_note: 全连接、卷积与残差网络上的初步实验已提供现象依据。不同观察所评价的对象不同，需要结合起来解释。
zh.feedback_return: 观察现象 → 检验理论条件 → 修正模型假设
zh.agenda_title:
以已有工具，
推进尚待解决的问题。
zh.agenda_intro: 具体模型中的结果为更一般的分析提供起点。研究计划进一步关注动态表示、非线性耦合与有利特征的形成条件。
established_items: 学习曲线、最优性、高维速率、饱和效应，以及固定表示下的风险等价。

理解局部近似的适用条件及其可能带来的泛化收益。
有利特征的形成与保持

terms: 候选特征映射集合，其中 Φ : 𝓧 → 𝓗。
